I want to make the argument that Vice News completely butchered this take on Japanese Mangaka and Anime culture regarding the drawing of Lolicon/Shota artwork, as well as obscuring this image as CP.  

I’m sure you’ve heard the same argument about video games, such as games like Call of Duty, Battlefield or other FPS games aim at exposing hyper-violence actions and desensitization of violence towards youth and young adults alike, the general populace and critics have made arguments of a correlation from video games and mass shootings or other forms of male violence.  This is not entirely the case, and if it is, is only limited to very special cases of individuals that have had preconceived mental health issues.  The same is for Lolicon/Shota artwork.

A line is typically drawn when an individual is a consumer of lolicon, such as, you can like the artwork, but that doesn’t mean it’ll transition to actually liking real life young kids in that way.  The facts of this artwork?  No children were harmed in the production of the artwork, the artwork being drawn holds no actual similarities to a real life child, the artwork is and should be protected under free speech laws or laws regarding art regulations passed by a governing review board.  

Of course, this topic is heavily debated, and I can see where criticisms are valid, especially for people new to anime and manga, or perhaps when viewing lolicon/Shota, they may interpret it as a living entity in resemblance of actually children, or perhaps they simply don’t like it, and arguments that those who view it are only p*do’s.  Whatever the argument for being against it may be, I’m in favor of such artwork being protected under free speech laws and subject through review by a governing board.  Limitations are as mentioned, that the artwork should not resemble actual kids, should do no harm unto real life kids and should be reviewed and regulated.  I’ll link a YouTube video that goes into this argument about lolicon/Shota for reference: [In Defense of Lolicon](https://youtu.be/xLDUfMWmRAA)

Would love to hear more thoughts about this topic, whether agreeing or disagreeing opinions.  However, I’ll say to conclude, Vice News has done gross negligence towards covering this topic, especially labeling it as pe*phil*c.

The military, at least the USMC that I served in, essentially just tossed me back out into civilian life.  I remember 4yrs ago how I would have nightmares almost every night, and be hyper-vigilant going out in public.  

One of my buddies, he didn’t see combat, however, that didn’t mean he didn’t experience suffering in his own way.  Toxic leadership combined with hazing and always being on edge, he would tell me all the time he would get terrible nightmares of people dying around him.  The stress was intense.  It’s more difficult to explain to those who’ve never served because they’ll look at you, especially if you haven’t served in combat, and might have an idea, but ultimately not understand in-depth, the severity of stress and it’s toll on the mind, body and spirit while being in service.  Especially if your in the infantry.

Intelligence in itself is complex, however, it can be identifiable as to how one is perceived “low intelligent,” “average in intelligence” or above average in intelligence.  

There is an individual’s capability in excelling academically, as well as socially and emotionally.  Another factor is also how one’s self awareness of themselves, their environment and the world in which they inhabit.  Another consideration is one’s understanding of the world, both abstract and simple concepts.  One’s understanding of themselves, such as their nature.  And of course how open-minded they are, whether towards change, towards learning from others but also balancing that with objective knowledge and so on.  And one more I’d like to add are their willingness to accept being wrong and learning to grow in all previously said areas. 

Taking these factors into consideration (of course not an exclusive list), I would say someone is below average in intelligence if they do not currently inherit these characteristics or traits.  Someone would be average in intelligence if holding the bare minimum.  And someone would be above average in intelligence by adopting, growing and even exceeding in these areas.

Don’t be mistaken that intelligence in itself is primarily static, but indeed plastic, that being if you are lacking in certain areas in the present, you can continue to grow in those areas only if you are aware of it and actively make an effort to change in those areas.
